description: Buddy-authored child-friendly core senses with a pinned British pronunciation evidence layer.

senses.definition: A business that keeps, lends and manages money.
senses.example: She put the money into her bank account.

senses.definition: The land along the side of a river or other water.
senses.example: We sat on the river bank and watched the ducks.

senses.definition: The short, loud sound a dog makes.
senses.example: The dog's bark made us look round.

senses.definition: The protective outer covering of a tree.
senses.example: The bark on the tree felt rough.

senses.definition: A small flying mammal that is usually active at night.
senses.example: A bat flew out of the cave at dusk.

senses.definition: A piece of sports equipment used to hit a ball.
senses.example: She swung the cricket bat and hit the ball.

senses.definition: The best result that has been achieved in an activity.
senses.example: The runner broke the school record.

senses.definition: To capture sound, pictures or information so they can be used later.
senses.example: We can record the birdsong and listen to it later.

senses.definition: To give something to someone in exchange for money.
senses.example: The shop sells bread and milk.

senses.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
senses.example: We go through the gate and follow the path.

senses.definition: To create, build or produce something.
senses.example: She made a paper boat.

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.
senses.example: The dog ran across the field.

senses.definition: To hold or support something while moving it from one place to another.
senses.example: She carries the bag to school each morning.

pronunciations.ipa: s t ˈɔː ɹ i z

senses.definition: An account of events, real or imagined, told to other people.
senses.example: We read a funny story before bed.

senses.definition: From one side, end or part of something to the other.
senses.example: We walked through the woods to the lake.

senses.definition: As much or as many as is needed.
senses.example: There was enough pizza for everyone.

senses.definition: A group of people who sing together.
senses.example: The school choir sang on the stage.

senses.definition: A boat used for sailing, racing or pleasure.
senses.example: The yacht sailed slowly across the bay.

senses.definition: A senior rank for an officer in an army.
senses.example: The colonel spoke to the soldiers.

pronunciations.ipa: f ˈəʊ t ə g ɹ ˌɑː f

senses.definition: A picture made with a camera.
senses.example: I took a photograph of the rainbow.

pronunciations.ipa: s t ˈeɪ ʃ ə n

senses.definition: A place where trains or buses stop so people can get on or off.
senses.example: We waited at the station for our train.

pronunciations.ipa: ɪ k s t ɹ ˈɔː d ɪ n ə ɹ i
ˌɛ k s t ɹ ə ˈɔː d ɪ n ə ɹ i

senses.definition: Very unusual, special or surprising.
senses.example: The view from the mountain was extraordinary.

senses.definition: The process plants use to make food from light, water and carbon dioxide.
senses.example: Plants use photosynthesis to make food using sunlight.

pronunciations.ipa: ˌɒ n ə m ˌæ t ə p ˈiː ə

senses.definition: The use of a word that sounds like the noise it describes.
senses.example: Buzz and hiss are examples of onomatopoeia.

senses.definition: A lucky or useful discovery made by chance.
senses.example: Finding the hidden beach by accident was serendipity.

senses.definition: Correct or true.
senses.example: Your answer is right, so move on to the next question.

senses.definition: The direction or side opposite left.
senses.example: Turn right at the end of the road.

senses.definition: In maths, an average found by adding the numbers and dividing by how many numbers there are.
senses.example: The mean of 4, 6 and 8 is 6.

senses.definition: To intend or want something to happen.
senses.example: I did not mean to knock over your drink.

senses.definition: Caring and helpful towards other people.
senses.example: It was kind of Sam to help the new pupil.

senses.definition: A type or sort of thing.
senses.example: What kind of animal is a dolphin?

senses.definition: In maths, a number that divides another number exactly with no remainder.
senses.example: Three is a factor of twelve.

senses.definition: One of the things that helps cause or affect a result.
senses.example: Weather was one factor in deciding where to hold the event.

senses.definition: Used to show that something is true even though another fact might make it seem surprising.
senses.example: Although it was raining, we still went for a walk.

senses.definition: Used to introduce an idea that contrasts with what was just said.
senses.example: The first route was shorter; however, the second was safer.

senses.definition: For that reason; used to show a result or conclusion.
senses.example: The path was flooded, therefore we took another route.

senses.definition: Except if something happens or is true.
senses.example: You cannot enter unless you have a ticket.

senses.definition: In the space that separates two people, places or things.
senses.example: The ball rolled between the two chairs.

senses.definition: At some time within an event or period of time.
senses.example: We stayed indoors during the storm.

senses.definition: Not having, using or doing something.
senses.example: She finished the puzzle without any help.

senses.definition: In the direction of someone or something.
senses.example: The dog ran towards the gate.
